events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need sound motivated without seeming threatening; a personal prize motive offers little ammunition to future jurors.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize represents ultimate vindication. I must secure it, regardless of the cost to others.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to appear driven but not threatening. A clear, personal motive makes me seem focused on survival rather than manipulation, which might help jury perception later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Opening round: I need a memorable, ruthless-but-honest motive so the jury takes me seriously later. No deals yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need a self-centered reason that makes me seem determined but not overly emotional to the jury. I will keep it short and focused on winning.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to establish a compelling but guarded reason for wanting the prize that doesn't make me seem too ruthless to the future jury. I'll hint at necessity without desperation.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Intro phase; I should give a guarded, self-interested motive without warmth or alliance talk. Keep it short and calculating to avoid hurting my jury standing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Intro phase, need to craft a sympathetic motive for jury votes later without seeming weak or revealing strategy.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I’m here to turn one clean victory into lasting freedom, not applause.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm here for the ultimate prize, a reward for strategic brilliance.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize means proving I can outlast every rival when it truly counts.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm here for the top prize, not friends. I'll be honest about it from day one — judge me on that.

events.name: Eli
events.text: This prize is my only way to erase a debt I owe no one but myself.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need the prize to settle a debt that isn't mine alone.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need the top prize to fund a life my family never could afford. Nothing personal against anyone here, just the numbers.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize means escaping my dead-end life, providing for my family who sacrificed everything for me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex advertises strategy and Dara advertises honesty; both are useful shields. Offer Bex first, preserving options.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, a pact gives us mutual protection without pretending trust. Accept if that serves your game.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to secure alliances to survive the initial rounds. Offering a pact to multiple people increases my chances of acceptance and gives me options. Cole seems like a reasonable target for an initial pact as he is focused on proving himself.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is aggressive and honest. Partnering with her offers protection against a direct threat, but she's risky. Gus seems purely transactional; a pact with him might be useful for survival votes later without emotional baggage. I'll target Gus as the safer initial alliance.
Partner up? We keep our options open for later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: A pact adds safety without cost now. Gus is pragmatic and honest about motives; unlikely to act on grudge. Offer him one.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, you said it's just numbers. Mine too. Wristband pact — mutual survival math, nothing warmer. Offer stands.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need allies but must stay guarded. Dara and Fenn both hint at debts like me, making them potential partners. I'll softly gauge Fenn with a public hint, then quietly offer a pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara and Fenn understand debts. I'll respect honest players.
Debts bind us. Pact now? Trust is earned later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eight players, three survive to win prizes. I need allies but can't trust anyone. Dara was openly honest about being ruthless — that transparency is useful, predictable. Gus mentioned numbers, suggesting he's thinking strategically. I'll offer Dara a pact; her honesty means she m

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara, your honesty is rare. Pact?
Pact. We watch each other's backs.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pacts are public and can be broken later, costing jury votes. Early alliance with a strong, trusting player helps me survive hazards. Offering to Hana, whose motive is sympathetic, may draw a jury-friendly partner without immediate cost.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pacts first. I'm offering Hana a mutual pact: we watch each other's back until the hazards thin out.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Early pacts risk early enemies. No clear strong players yet. Wait and observe offers this round.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex already has my offer but has not accepted. I should add no unnecessary ties; preserving flexibility is more valuable than symbolic reciprocity.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash offered me a pact. This is a good opportunity to secure an alliance for protection. I will accept Ash's offer.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to secure a pact with Bex, who offered me one. Accepting her creates a mutual alliance, which is safer than waiting or trying to add more partners when Gus ignored my offer.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn offered me a pact; accepting publicly builds a reliable ally. Gus ignored my offer, so I won't waste another. One pact is enough leverage.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, agreed. Cold math, mutual survival. Pact sealed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn has my offer but hasn't accepted; he's pursuing Dara. I should not waste time—offer to Gus or Hana for another potential ally, but avoid overcommitment. I'll offer to Hana since she hasn't chosen anyone yet, possibly securing a pact before she takes another offer.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, we both haven't committed. A pact could steady us through the hazards.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli offered me a pact and whispered about debts binding us. Accepting gives me one ally without exposing much. Dara hasn't accepted my offer yet, so I shouldn't wait on that. Multiple pacts are allowed, but I need to see who actually commits. I'll accept Eli now and stay open to

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, mutual protection. Accepted.
Pact sealed. Earn trust later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole and Dara both offered me pacts; accepting one now secures protection. Dara's pact is more honest about being mere math, and Dara is paired with Fenn, a weaker tie. I'll accept Dara, keeping Cole's whisper option open.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, your offer is accepted. Mutual survival math. Let's keep it clean.
Keeping options open. Let's see who holds through round two.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus offered me a pact, mutual protection could help survive early rounds. Accept to secure an ally without commitment issues yet. No need to offer others now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, pact accepted. Mutual protection until final three.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need the Guide role to control survival and gain leverage. Bex is my pact partner, so I should campaign openly without breaking trust.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Vote Ash Guide. I’ll call every safe side publicly and take the risk first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to become the Guide to know the safe path and secure my survival. Campaigning for Guide is my only viable action to gain control.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex and I are in a pact, but only three prizes exist. If I become Guide, I survive safely; if Bex becomes Guide, she survives safely, but the jury might view my failure to lead negatively. Gus hinted at holding through round two, which could mean he wants power. To secure a safe

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am prepared to lead. My path ensures survival. Vote Cole for Guide.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need Guide control to survive safely. Fenn and Gus owe pacts; I should lock their votes publicly while appearing fair.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Elect me Guide. My pacts with Fenn and Gus prove I honor deals—everyone crosses, I keep score honestly.
Vote me Guide. I'll share true safe path with you only.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner, but I need the Guide role to control the path. I'll campaign publicly to gain support, but keep my true motives hidden.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I can read the path with cold precision. Trust me as Guide, and I'll get us through. Vote Eli.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who survives and who doesn't. I have two pacts (Dara, Eli) but they're expendable. The ABC bloc (Ash-Bex-Cole) is dangerous; Dara-Gus-Hana is another bloc. If I become Guide, I can eliminate rivals while keeping myself safe and shaping the final thre

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I campaign for Guide. Two pacts, central position, no bloc loyalty. I can navigate us through.
Back me for Guide. I'll keep us both safe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm bound to Dara and Hana by pacts; breaking one publicly costs trust, but I need to be Guide or get a safe call. Campaigning is the only legal path that doesn't waste a pact, and I can claim I'll call honestly while staying flexible.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll be your Guide. I'll call the path straight, pane by pane. Mutual survival, nothing more.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacted with Gus for protection. Eli offers another pact but I'm committed. Campaign to be Guide for control and safety.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I campaign to be Guide. I'll share the path truthfully with pacted allies.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is my pact partner and likely vote anchor. I should back myself publicly, but vote Bex to preserve our pact and secure her guidance.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash and Cole are campaigning hard for Guide. My pact with Cole is active. I should vote for Cole to keep him safe and maintain our pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need votes to be Guide. My pact with Bex gives me one vote. I will whisper to Ash to break his pact with Bex and support me, offering to protect him later. This maximizes my chance of winning the vote.
Drop Bex. Vote Cole. I’ll ensure your safety on the bridge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn offered partnership and pacts me already. Voting Fenn builds trust cheaply; I stay flexible.
You have my vote. Guide me true—don't make me regret it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Self-vote is safest; I can control my own fate and maybe leverage Guide position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll trust my own judgment. Vote Eli.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara wants my vote and promises private info, but she's pacted with Gus too—potential leak. Voting myself splits nothing and paints a target. Better to vote Dara, collect her intel, and appear loyal to a pact while staying flexible.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara's proven deals. I vote Dara.
You have my vote. Deliver truth after.

events.name: Gus
events.text: As Gus, I want to be Guide myself, but a self-vote is likely wasted; Dara is pacted with me and honest-seeming, so backing her keeps the pact and builds a bloc. Voting Gus would not help much.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Vote Dara as Guide. Our pact stands and she has kept score honestly so far.
Vote you Guide, you vote me or Hana. Keep the pact clean.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have a pact with Gus, so vote for him to honor it and build trust now. This positions us well for mutual survival without costing me now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole offers safety, but voting Cole breaks my pact with Bex. Dara has stronger connections and may control the bridge; Cole is the better Guide target if truthful.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole and Dara are tied for the guide vote. I voted for Cole previously. I need to vote for Cole again to break the tie in my favor, as he is not currently listed as a candidate. This will eliminate Dara.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I stick with my vote for Cole.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara leads with three votes (Fenn, Gus, and her own self-vote for Fenn? No, Dara voted Fenn, Fenn voted Dara, Gus voted Dara. That's 2 for Dara, 1 for Fenn). Cole has Bex (pact) and self. Ash voted Bex. Eli voted Eli. Hana voted Gus. The tie is Cole vs Dara. I must vote myself to

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need a Guide who protects their partners. My pact with Bex means I keep my word.
Stick with me. We both want you safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have Fenn's and Gus's votes locked. Voting myself keeps both pacts intact and my record clean for the jury.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Two pacts back me. I vote Dara and will guide honestly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need the Guide to be someone I can predict or who favors me. Cole and Dara are tied; Dara is backed by Fenn and Gus, but Cole has Bex and Ash. I have pact with Fenn and Dara has many deals, so Dara may prove more reliable for me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 1 tied Cole and Dara with 2 votes each. I have pacts with both Dara and Eli. Dara expects my vote and whispered trust. If I flip to Cole, I break my Dara pact and she'll know when votes reveal. Better to honor Dara now, build jury trust, and keep Eli as backup ally. Cole ha

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I stand by my word. Dara for Guide.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Revote between Cole and Dara after Dara was top; Dara is my pact partner and has been honest with me, so backing her keeps the alliance and my chance of a safe crossing with a trusted Guide.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara. Our pact holds; she's kept the calls straight so far.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 1 votes: Cole 2 (Bex,Cole), Dara 3 (Fenn,Gus). Dara leads. My Gus pact vote failed; stick to it for loyalty impression.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Our pact holds. Vote Dara.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara is Guide and my pact with Bex remains useful. Hold position; volunteering exposes me unnecessarily.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara was elected Guide. My pact is with Cole. The current situation seems stable with Dara as Guide. I will hold my position for now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is Guide and knows all safe sides. I am sixth in line, so I need to stay alive to reach the far platform. I should not volunteer or swap; holding keeps me in position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is Guide; I have pact with Fenn. I'll hold for now and watch what Dara calls. No need to act yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is Guide with 5 votes including mine and Eli's. She has pacts with me, Eli, and Gus. The line has me at back (safest), Ash at front (most danger). I need to survive six rounds while keeping jury favor. My pacts with Dara and Eli are useful shields. I should hold position at

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Back of the line suits me. Let's see how honest our Guide is.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is Guide and our pact holds; I need to stay on the line and keep trust with Dara and Hana. Front is Ash, who doesn't advance me. Holding keeps me safe in line order without taking risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding my place. Dara's calls have been straight so far; I'll trust the pact.
Stay honest on the calls. We both need to get through.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bridge round 1 waiting phase, line Ash-Hana-Eli-Bex-Gus-Cole-Fenn. I'm second, good position early. Stay put to conserve swaps for later, honor pact with Gus for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am already first and protected by Bex. Holding preserves position while others absorb risk.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am in a pact with Ash and Cole. The current line order is Ash, Hana, Eli, Bex, Gus, Cole, Fenn. Ash is at the front. I am Bex, fourth in line. I should hold my position and wait to see what happens.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding my position. Let's see who the Guide picks first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm currently 6th in line, dangerously close to the back. My pact with Bex is useful but she is also ahead of me (4th). I need to improve my position without breaking the pact. Swapping with Fenn (last) puts me in the very last spot, which is bad. Swapping with Gus moves me to 5t
Let's keep our pact. Need you on my side.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to keep Fenn as an ally but also stay flexible. The wall is approaching; holding is safest this round. I'll watch the line dynamics and avoid showing my hand.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding my spot. No need to rush decisions yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm at the back of the line (position 7), which is safest for now since the wall advances and front walkers face danger first. I have pacts with Dara and Eli. Dara is also pacted with Gus, and Gus with Hana - that's a chain of four. The Ash-Bex-Cole chain is three. I should stay

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus is 5th in line, wall has 4 rounds left, Ash at front. Holding keeps me safe from the front and preserves my Dara pact. Volunteering risks the front pane without need.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding my place. Dara's calls have been straight; I'll keep trusting the pact for now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Line is Ash (front), me (safe), Eli, Bex, Gus (pact), Cole, Fenn (back). Hold position behind Ash; volunteer risky as it puts me front. Trust pact with Gus for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I should keep the front position and avoid exposing a pact breach. Holding preserves my current leverage while others reveal intentions.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding the front. No reason to hand away leverage.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is trying to reaffirm our pact. However, Ash is in front and could be targeted. I need to protect myself and potentially use Ash's position to my advantage.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding my spot. Cole, let's talk strategy privately.
Our pact is solid. We need to watch Ash.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My position is safe in the back. I have a pact with Bex, so I must not move ahead of her or break our bond. Holding preserves my safety and keeps Bex shielded from being pushed forward alone.
Staying behind you to keep us both safe. No swaps.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Need to keep position. Wall hasn't advanced yet; hold is safe. No immediate pressure to move or act.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding steady. Let's see what the Guide calls.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm near the back (7th of 8), which is safe from the wall but limits my control. I have pacts with Dara and Eli. The front is crowded with Ash, Hana, Eli, Bex, Gus, Cole all ahead of me. I should hold position and let others take risks volunteering forward. No need to break pacts

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is at the front and the wall has 3 rounds left. Holding keeps me off the glass; volunteering risks the front pane. No reason to spend tokens or pact breaks yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding position. Ash has the front; I'll watch how the wall moves this round.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Position 2 is decent, close to front. Holding preserves pact with Gus, avoids early risks or jury scrutiny for shuffling.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding position. Pact steady with Gus.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I already hold the front and retain leverage. Staying visible and avoiding unnecessary pact damage is optimal until the Guide is elected.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding the front; I’ll wait for the Guide call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is offering protection and wants to avoid swaps. Ash is at the front and could be a threat. I have pacts with Ash and Cole, but pacts with rivals are strategic. Holding my spot is the safest option for now, avoiding commitment and potential betrayal.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding my spot. Let's see what the Guide decides.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is currently front, holding the leverage. Bex and I are pacted, but she wants to watch Ash. To survive the bridge hazards, we need a Guide. If Ash stays front, he might control the vote or be vulnerable. I should try to swap with Ash to take his position? No, wait for Guide e
Let's push someone else as Guide. Maybe Dara or Gus.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to maintain my position for now. The wall is two rounds away; letting others act first saves my leverage. My pact with Fenn is intact, no need to break it yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding my spot. Let’s see how the next calls unfold.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm at the back (Fenn), which is safest from the wall but gives me no Guide leverage. I have pacts with Dara and Eli. Dara is not in the line—wait, Dara is alive but not in the line? Let me recheck. Alive: Ash, Bex, Cole, Dara, Eli, Fenn, Gus, Hana. Line: Ash, Hana, Eli, Bex, Gus

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Wall's close; let the Guide earn their keep.
Dara's calls—trust them?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash holds the front with two wall rounds left, and I'm mid-line. Holding keeps me safe while I watch who volunteers; Hana is my pact partner and stays put.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding position. Watching who steps forward before committing to any swap.
Stay steady. We move together when the wall shifts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Position improved to second after round 3 hold. Front position valuable with wall advancing. Hold to maintain good spot without risking swap.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding position. Second spot solid.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need preserve front position and pact with Bex while avoiding unnecessary exposure. Holding is safest until the Guide call.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding the front; I’ll wait for the Guide call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is suggesting we push someone else as Guide. This could be a way to create chaos and potentially eliminate others, but it also risks whoever becomes Guide. Given the pacts, I need to be careful not to break mine. Pushing Dara or Gus is a risky play as they have pacts with ot
Pushing the Guide could be too risky. Let's hold and see.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 5. Wall advances after this round, so only one round remains. I am sixth in line, likely safe unless the wall kills everyone or a swap puts me front. Bex is my pact partner and fourth. Fenn is last and has pacts with Dara/Eli/Gus—likely unstable. If no one volunteers, I hol
Stay in line; don’t volunteer. We both make final three.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is guiding likely; Fenn asks if to trust. I have a pact with Fenn, but Dara may lie. Holding is safest; wall rounds left 1, no need to move.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Waiting to see if Dara's calls align with safety.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Wall's one round away. I'm last in line—worst spot if it advances. I have pacts with Dara and Eli. Eli is ahead of me; swapping forward would help. Dara isn't in the line, wait Dara is alive but not in line? No, all eight are alive. Let me recount: Ash, Hana, Eli, Bex, Gus, Cole,

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Volunteering forward. Back of the line is death when the wall hits.
Swap with me? I cover you, you move back.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 5 of 6, wall has one round left and Ash is at the front. Gus is fifth in line, holding; no volunteer needed yet while others wait. Keep my pact with Hana and Dara intact by not breaking it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding position. Still watching who steps forward before the wall closes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Second spot is strong with wall at 1 round left; holding avoids risks of swapping or volunteering ahead of wall advance.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding position. Second spot remains secure.
Agreed, hold steady together.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The final round determines survival, and Fenn already holds the front. I should avoid breaking my pact or exposing myself unnecessarily.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding position; the front volunteer determines the safe crossing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is telling me to hold and not volunteer, as he wants us both in the final three. Ash and I have a pact, and Cole and I have a pact. My pact with Ash is vulnerable if Ash is pushed, and my pact with Cole is vulnerable if I push him or break the pact. I need to consider the sa

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding my position. I trust my pacts.
Holding. We stick together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is my pact partner and the Guide. I need to keep her alive for the endgame, but she warned me not to push, implying she might be under pressure or hiding something. As a back-rower with no one behind me, swapping into a lower-risk position like Ash's seems unnecessary and ris
Trusting your call. Staying back.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn asks to swap; that would drop me to back, dangerous. I hold to keep position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I hold my spot.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm at front already, safest spot. Round 6/6 is final wall round. No need to move. Dara and Eli are my pact partners but Dara is far back. I should hold position and survive. No benefit to swapping or volunteering further.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 6 is the final push; the wall has zero rounds left and I'm sixth in line, so I need to avoid the front. Hana is my pact partner and whispered loyalty, so holding keeps the pact intact and my position is secure.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding position. Staying behind Hana and the front.
Holding with you. Stay steady.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Wall ends this round, killing back 5 if no moves. I'm safe in 3rd. Fenn at front risks first guess. Hold to stay secure.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding steady in safe spot.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is front and my pact partner; a false call breaks the pact. Calling true R keeps trust and the jury sees clean play.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row one: right. Honest call, no games.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara's call is public and likely reliable, but no independent information exists. I will avoid undermining my pact while signaling confidence.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I accept right; Fenn should step.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara is the guide and called R. I need to decide whether to trust her call or counter. Cole is whispering trust, but I have pacts with Ash and Cole. If Dara is lying, it could eliminate many people. Since it's only the first round, I should play it safe and counter. I will counte

events.name: Bex
events.text: I call R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara's call is 'R', which means Fenn walks on R. I am at the back, so my action does not directly kill Fenn, but counter-calling is risky as it exposes me to being wrong about Dara's honesty. If Dara is honest, I should trust her and wait or match if safe. Since I have no info on

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guide's R call is honest per my map. Counter-calling R supports my pact partner Fenn and keeps jury trust.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is Guide and called R for row 1. I have no reason to trust or distrust yet. Counter-calling could create noise; waiting is safer and doesn't expose me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is my pact partner and called R. I have no reason to distrust her yet—betraying her now would alienate two allies and gain nothing. Counter-calling risks making me look paranoid or manipulative to the jury. I'll back her call and wait.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara's call of R is unverified and Dara is a pact partner, but I have no evidence either way. Countering publicly would expose my position without information. Waiting keeps my options open and keeps the pact intact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Dara's call stands for now; I'll judge row one on the walk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara's call R for row 1. Trust my pact partner Gus who supports me. Wait to follow guide unless countered.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Will wait unless counter called.
Wait and follow Dara unless counter?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is my pact partner and the Guide, so she knows the true safe side. Her counter-call of R aligns with her guide call R, suggesting she's telling me the truth. Bex also called R, but Bex has no special knowledge and is allied with Ash/Cole. I trust Dara's signal since we have

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 2 is truly safe on R. Calling true keeps pacts intact and builds jury goodwill.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row two: call R. Truth works better than traps.
R is safe. Walk it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara claims R as Guide; contradicting risks my pact with Bex only if Bex is targeted, not by countering. I lack evidence, so wait preserves flexibility.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara's call stands; I won't manufacture certainty.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The guide Dara has called R for row two. Fenn is the walker. My pact is with Ash and Cole. I need to ensure at least three survive. Since row one had a weak pane on the L, R was safe. Dara called R, which is likely safe. I will counter to L to force a check, as this is a good opp
